title: One country's engineers now run rooms they were never guaranteed a seat in. September 21, 2026.
excerpt: From an Adobe CEO handoff between two IIT graduates to a blind civil servant who cracked the UPSC without coaching, September 21's five stories are about the credential nobody can revoke: having actually done the work.
bodyHtml:
None of today's five subjects were handed their seat. Each one built the case for it first, then walked in.

India is paying up to ₹14 crore each to bring its scientists home

For decades, India's best researchers left and rarely came back. In June 2026, the government launched the PM Research Chair Scheme - a ₹200 crore program aiming to bring more than 120 Indian-origin researchers abroad back into Indian institutions, with packages of up to ₹14 crore each covering salary, lab setup and research funding. The goal isn't filling vacant posts; it's pulling top-tier research talent back into Indian labs, putting a price on reversing a decades-long, one-directional flow.

September 21, 1994: the industrialist who called himself "Gandhi's coolie"

Ramkrishna Bajaj died in Mumbai on September 21, 1994, at age 70. Born in Wardha in 1923 into the family that built the Bajaj Group, he chose jail over comfort first - joining Satyagraha at 17 and spending years imprisoned during the Quit India Movement alongside mentors including Gandhi and Vinoba Bhave. He ran Bajaj Group and Bajaj Electricals while simultaneously leading FICCI, the Indian Merchants' Chamber and the Maharashtra Chamber of Commerce - and his motto, "Trust in Quality and Business Ethics," became so associated with him that industry named India's answer to the Malcolm Baldrige Award after him in 1996.

One IIT campus, two Adobe CEOs, one relay baton

Adobe's board has named Anil Chakravarthy - a B.Tech graduate of IIT (BHU) Varanasi who moved to the US at 21 for MIT - as the company's next President and CEO, effective December 1, 2026. He succeeds Shantanu Narayen, himself Indian-origin, who becomes Executive Chair. Chakravarthy joined Adobe in 2020, built its Customer Experience business past $1 billion in quarterly revenue, and led the acquisitions of Workfront and Semrush - making this the second consecutive Indian-origin CEO to lead a company guiding toward $26 billion in annual revenue.

Ten Indians. One 246-year-old American academy. Same year.

The American Academy of Arts and Sciences - founded in 1780, whose past members include Einstein and Darwin - named its 2026 class of new members on April 22. Among the 252 leaders elected: ten are Indian-origin professionals living and working in the US, including former White House science chief Arati Prabhakar, former Infosys CEO Vishal Sikka and Girls Who Code founder Reshma Saujani. Separately, theoretical physicist Ashoke Sen was elected an International Honorary Member representing India, one of only a handful chosen from 14 countries worldwide.

 

She lost her sight in childhood. She became the officer running the show.

Pranjal Patil, from Ulhasnagar, Maharashtra, lost her eyesight in childhood and studied at a school for the blind before earning a postgraduate degree from Jawaharlal Nehru University. She cracked the UPSC Civil Services Examination without any coaching, using text-to-speech software to study, improving from rank 744 in 2016 to rank 124 in 2017. In 2018 she became India's first fully visually-impaired woman IAS officer, later serving as Sub-Collector of Thiruvananthapuram.

Five stories, one thread: a research package offered before the scientist says yes, an award named after a man's conscience two years after his death, a company handed to a second engineer from the same institute that trained the first, an academy seat earned in a system that owed nobody anything, and a civil service rank cracked without a single coaching class. Nothing here was inherited. Each one was built, then proven, then finally recognized - in that order, never the reverse.

coverHeadlines: For decades, India's best researchers left and rarely came back. In June 2026, the government put ₹200 crore on the table to reverse that.
September 21, 1994: India lost the industrialist who called himself "Gandhi's coolie" - and left behind a blueprint for honest business.
She lost her sight in childhood. Two decades later, she became the officer running the show.
2026: An Indian-origin engineer is about to run Adobe for the second time in a row.
Ten Indians. One 246-year-old American academy. Same year.
